summary:
AEGIS (Autonomous Crew Health) is a crew-facing health and readiness tool for long-duration space missions. Astronauts log sleep, fatigue, mood, and heart rate, compare those signals to their own early-mission baseline, complete a short in-browser reaction-time assessment, and receive Ready/Caution/Not recommended guidance before high-stakes tasks such as EVA.

It addresses the challenge by helping crews spot early performance changes themselves when ground support may be delayed. NASA OSDR RR-1 environmental data (cabin CO₂, temperature, humidity) is cached offline and used as an environmental stressor in advisories, forecasts, Mission Replay, and What-If scenarios. Crew health data is simulated from published ranges to protect medical privacy.

AEGIS matters because deep-space crews need timely, personal decisions rather than waiting on Earth or relying on fleet averages. It is an advisory prototype, not a clinical diagnostic system.
details:
How It Works

AEGIS (Astronaut Environmental & General Intelligence System) is an offline-first, AI-assisted astronaut health monitoring and mission readiness platform designed to strengthen crew autonomy during long-duration space missions. By combining personalized health tracking, machine learning, NASA environmental data, and operational decision support, AEGIS helps astronauts identify potential performance declines before critical mission activities.

1. Daily Health Monitoring and Cognitive Assessments

Through the Today dashboard, astronauts record sleep, fatigue, mood, and optional resting heart rate. The Assessments module provides an interactive reaction-time test and symptom checklist.

AEGIS compares these measurements against individualized baselines established from approximately the first 14 days of mission history. Statistical analysis identifies unusual deviations and sustained trends that may indicate changes in performance.

Today Screen:

Assessments Screen:

2. Machine Learning and Predictive Analytics

AEGIS uses scikit-learn Ridge regression to forecast next-day reaction time using sleep duration, recent reaction-time trends, resting heart-rate deviations, fatigue, and cabin CO₂ measurements.

The model uses standardized features and a chronological 75/25 training and evaluation split to avoid training on future observations. When insufficient data is available, a rolling-mean persistence model provides fallback predictions.

The Trends & Forecasts dashboard visualizes personalized baselines, historical changes, and illustrative 24-hour cognitive performance forecasts.

Trends & Forecasts Screen:

3. Interactive Astronaut Digital Twin

AEGIS features an interactive Astronaut Digital Twin that visualizes cognitive, cardiopulmonary, and fatigue-related indicators through a color-coded body model.

Green, amber, and red indicators highlight deviations from personal baselines, while integrated forecasts and historical trends provide an intuitive overview of astronaut well-being.

Digital Twin Screen:

4. Mission Readiness Gate

The Readiness Gate translates physiological trends, cognitive assessments, and fatigue indicators into operational recommendations before activities such as EVAs, docking, and maintenance.

Using transparent, rule-based logic, AEGIS assigns one of three advisory classifications:

  • Ready: No significant concerns detected.
  • Caution: Potential performance concerns require attention.
  • Not Recommended: Significant warning indicators suggest additional evaluation before proceeding.

Each classification includes explanations and recommended next steps, helping astronauts make informed decisions without immediate ground support.

Readiness Gate Screen:

5. What-If Simulator and NASA Mission Replay

The What-If Simulator allows astronauts to adjust sleep, fatigue, and cabin CO₂ conditions to explore how hypothetical changes might influence predicted reaction-time performance.

What-If Simulator Screen:

NASA Mission Replay integrates historical environmental and radiation observations from NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), including RR-1 mission data. Statistical anomaly detection highlights unusual CO₂, temperature, and humidity patterns, demonstrating how historical spacecraft conditions can inform environmental monitoring.

NASA Mission Replay Screen:

6. Offline-First Telemetry and Communications

AEGIS operates locally without requiring continuous internet access. Its Telemetry & Relay module uses AES-GCM encryption to protect health summaries and queues reports for simulated delayed transmission to ground control.

Historical NASA datasets are cached locally in SQLite, enabling offline access to environmental observations and supporting continued operation during communication disruptions.

Telemetry & Relay Screen:

Benefits and Intended Impact

As astronauts travel farther from Earth, communication delays, isolation, altered gravity, radiation, and environmental stressors create growing challenges for crew health and mission safety.

AEGIS addresses these challenges by integrating personalized monitoring, cognitive forecasting, and mission readiness assessment into one accessible platform.

By identifying potential performance changes earlier, visualizing complex health information, and providing explainable operational advisories, AEGIS aims to strengthen astronaut autonomy, improve situational awareness, and support safer decision-making during deep-space missions.

Its offline-first architecture also makes the approach relevant to other isolated environments, including submarines, polar research stations, and remote expeditions.

AEGIS is a decision-support prototype, not a clinically validated diagnostic system. Cognitive forecasts are illustrative, crew health histories are simulated, and NASA environmental observations are historical mission data.

Tools and Technology Stack

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts
  • Backend: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, SQLite
  • Machine Learning: Python, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn Ridge regression, StandardScaler
  • NASA Data: NASA OSDR EDA APIs, historical RR-1 environmental and radiation observations, local caching
  • Security: AES-GCM encryption, locally queued telemetry, simulated delayed uplink
  • Health Data: Simulated astronaut physiological and psychological measurements informed by published reference ranges

AEGIS runs locally without continuous cloud connectivity, supporting autonomous operation in communication-constrained environments.

Creativity and Design Choices

AEGIS goes beyond traditional health dashboards by connecting personalized monitoring, predictive machine learning, environmental intelligence, and operational decision support into one unified platform.

Its key innovations include:

  • Personalized Baselines: Detecting changes relative to each astronaut's typical health and performance rather than relying exclusively on generalized thresholds.
  • Predictive Intelligence: Forecasting next-day reaction time using Ridge regression and recent physiological and environmental trends.
  • Interactive Digital Twin: Translating complex health indicators into an intuitive, color-coded visualization.
  • Mission-Aware Recommendations: Connecting performance changes to explainable readiness advisories for EVAs, docking, and maintenance.
  • Real NASA Data Integration: Incorporating historical RR-1 environmental and radiation observations alongside clearly identified simulated crew health data.
  • Offline-First Design: Supporting local analytics, encrypted reporting, and simulated delayed communications without depending on continuous Earth connectivity.

Its core workflow: Daily Check-In → Cognitive Assessment → Digital Twin → Readiness Gate demonstrates how intelligent, accessible tools could support astronaut independence and safety during future deep-space exploration.
